A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LUDVIG. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and shared content can be matched despite substantial expansion and relocation in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original NVOS and SPIn-NeRF segmentation results, ablations and qualitative visualizations in Tables 1–3 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds LERF localization and segmentation experiments, runtime measurements and qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: v2 adds a CLIP pipeline that uplifts multiscale embeddings, refines them through DINOv2-guided diffusion, and performs text-query localization and SAM segmentation. v1 used diffusion for segmentation weights. The basic aggregation remains unchanged, but v2 also revises the written graph-weighting and diffusion-update rules.

E1.justification: Beyond retained NVOS and SPIn-NeRF segmentation, v2 evaluates language-query localization and segmentation on LangSplat's extended LERF benchmark, covering ramen, figurines, teatime and waldo. Appendix C.1 also adds object-removal scene-editing demonstrations.

E2.justification: v2 adds LERF and LangSplat comparisons in Table 3, plus qualitative comparisons with N3F and GaussianEditor in Figures 7–9; N3F panels are sourced from prior work. Table 2 additionally includes SA3D-TRF on SPIn-NeRF. Its NVOS entry corresponds to the SA3D comparison already present in v1.

E3.justification: The added LERF evaluation introduces localization accuracy, text-relevancy-based bandwidth selection, argmax localization, SAM/Otsu segmentation and runtime accounting that includes feature generation and feature training. Existing NVOS/SPIn-NeRF reference-frame evaluation and tuning are retained. Newly specified numerical SAM prompt thresholds document existing procedures rather than establish changed settings.

E4.justification: The original segmentation ablation is retained as v2 Table 6. New analyses include a runtime breakdown in B.2, scene-editing and feature-quality comparisons with N3F in C.1–C.2, an aggregation-normalization comparison with GaussianEditor in C.3, and qualitative CLIP-refinement and localization analyses in C.4.

E5.justification: Both Section 5.1 passages state averaging over three independent runs. Neither version reports confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests or specific seeds. The added result entries do not establish a changed statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: v1 Tables 1–3 are numerically preserved in v2 Tables 4–6. New results include SA3D-TRF's 93.7 SPIn-NeRF IoU and Table 3's LERF evaluation: LUDVIG reports 85.1 localization accuracy, 61.3 segmentation IoU and 9 minutes, versus LangSplat's 84.3, 51.4 and 105 minutes. Additional qualitative findings and component timings are reported; these are additions, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: The aggregation equations and single-gradient-step derivation remain. The graph definition changes from v1's exponential local-plus-unary weighting to v2's similarity product with inverse-square-root unary factors at both endpoints; v2 also explicitly normalizes each diffusion iterate. This is a localized formal revision, without a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v2 broadens the central contribution to diffusion-based feature enrichment across segmentation and language-query tasks. Its third listed contribution changes from high-resolution rendered feature maps to DINOv2-guided CLIP enrichment and competitive open-vocabulary localization. The earlier feature-map capability remains described in Section 3.2.

C2.justification: Beyond the retained specular-reconstruction discussion, v2 identifies blurred/high-frequency reconstruction difficulties and bandwidth-search overhead in Section 6. Appendix C adds interpretations of CLIP semantic refinement, unseen-region artifacts after object removal, and LangSplat's localization-precision versus processing-cost tradeoff. Earlier segmentation failure analyses are largely retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies SAM prompt-selection thresholds of 0.4 for SPIn-NeRF and 1 for NVOS, explains that W and D are not explicitly constructed, and documents OpenCLIP ViT-B/16, relevancy smoothing and selection parameters, GPU hardware and component runtimes. Much of the earlier SAM/DINO segmentation detail is relocated rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through dedicated discussions of direct uplifting, including OpenGaussian and Semantic Gaussians, and CLIP-based localization, including LangSplat. It adds spectral-graph and CLIP-DINOiser connections and explicitly positions DINO-guided refinement directly in 3D against earlier 2D refinement and optimization-based approaches.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution narrative are substantially rewritten. Graph diffusion moves from segmentation-specific Section 4.3 to general Section 3.3, detailed downstream procedures and per-scene discussions move into Appendices A/B, the main experimental narrative is condensed, and a concluding remarks and limitations section is added.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the main per-scene tables with compact benchmark and ablation summaries while preserving the originals as Appendix Tables 4–6. It adds LERF Table 3, the sliding-window diagram in Figure 4 and comparison/refinement/localization Figures 7–11. Earlier visualizations are retained and redistributed, including placing Figures 2 and 3 together.

improvement.justification: v1's efficiency and generality claims rested mainly on segmentation experiments and an isolated uplifting time. v2 substantially strengthens their support through CLIP/LERF evaluation, feature-processing runtime comparisons and qualitative checks of aggregation and refinement. Added settings and concrete limitations make the claims easier to assess. The revised unary weighting remains insufficiently reconciled with its foreground-similarity explanation, but the overall evidential gains are substantial.
